name: Game switch: blur reveal, the logo becomes the game tag
when: The footage changes game: the cut from GTA VI footage to another game's footage (San Andreas, GTA IV, Red Dead 2), and the cut back to GTA VI after it (owner, 17 Nov 2026: never a direct cut between two games). One in and one out per run of another game's shots, the same variant both ways (series). The incoming game's logo (on the way back: the GTA VI logo) comes from assets/logos/ through `game`; a logo is never drawn or invented. The blur reveal doubles as the game tag: going to another game its logo lands over the blurred incoming shot, then glides to the corner and stays (`dock` corner), so no separate gametag is needed for that run; coming back to GTA VI, `dock` none and the logo lifts away with the blur.
anchor: Mount it over the project's own hard cut between the two games' shots: start the scene `cut` (0.3 s) before the cut. The blur clears at `clear`; with `dock` corner the logo stays in the corner until `out`, the last frame of that game's footage.
placement: Keep the project's footage as a plain hard cut. Mount the scene above both with make_scene --start <cut - 0.3>. `veil` is the incoming shot itself, blurred and pre-rolled so it lines up with the sharp shot underneath: `@clip <the incoming shot's source> <its in-point - cut> <clear + 0.5> | gblur=sigma=30:steps=2` (build_video bakes it). The sharp shot underneath must start at the cut at that same in-point.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme (only the dim and the year's colour change)
vars.game: the incoming game, as logos.json names it (going back: Grand Theft Auto VI)
vars.logo: its logo file: filled from assets/logos/ by build_video.mjs when `game` is listed there
vars.logo_cx: the logo's visual centre in logo widths from its image centre (+ = right), so the year centres on the artwork, not on the image box (owner, 17 Nov 2026: the 2026 looked off-centre under the GTA VI logo). build_video.mjs fills it from assets/logos/logos.json (cx); calling make_scene yourself, pass that cx (GTA VI 0.091)
vars.year: its release year, under the logo until the blur clears; empty = none
vars.veil: the incoming shot, blurred, pre-rolled by `cut` (see placement)
vars.big: the logo's width in px in the centre (760)
vars.width: the logo's width in px in the corner (400 for a wide wordmark)
vars.dock: corner (going to another game: the logo stays as its tag) or none (back to GTA VI: it lifts away)
vars.cut: seconds after the start: the hard cut under the veil (0.3)
vars.clear: seconds after the start: when the blur clears (1.15)
vars.out: seconds after the start: when the corner logo leaves (the scene ends 0.23 s later); land it on the last frame of that game's footage. With dock none (back to GTA VI) it is not used: give make_scene --duration <clear + 0.33> (1.48 with the defaults)

lab: Not validated yet (built 17 Nov 2026 for the owner's note: 'when we clearly change game, a small clean transition in, and another one to come back to GTA 6'). Not in catalogue.md until he picks A, B or C.
